title: Universality of critical quench autocorrelations in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model

issues.location: Sections 3, 4, 7, 8 (edge cap estimates, warming theorem, history cutoffs, clock-score projections)
issues.description: Not a demonstrated error; this is a coverage caveat. These sections hold most of the technical weight: the low-scale cap and variance estimates, the warming entropy, kernel and log-moment bounds with exponent 1.54, and the score table with its n^{-0.0007} gain at fourth order that the Lindeberg step needs. I only spot-checked them for internal consistency of exponents (5/3-xi profile gives entropy exponent at most 1.523, under 1.54; the 1.662 profile gives kernel exponent 1.51; semicircle-edge constants b_0=4/(3pi) and 2b_0 check out). I did not verify them line by line. The whole argument also leans heavily on the companion stationary paper FUA (Prop 2.3, Cor 3.3, Lemma 2.5/3.2, Prop 5.1, Thm 6.8, Prop 9.2), which I did not audit.
issues.evidence: Theorem 4.1 (warm:entropy, warm:kernel); Proposition 4.2 profiles L^{5/3-xi}, L^{1.662}/L^{1.162}; score table (repl:score-table) with extra factors n^{-0.01}, n^{-0.001}, n^{-0.0007} when D >= T n^{-0.005}

coverage: I read the introduction and main theorem, Section 2 (stationary inputs and conventions), all of Section 5 (Gaussian subsequential limits, uniform-start escape estimate), all of Section 6 (entrance selection), the statement and opening of Section 9 plus the entrywise replacement and tightness transfer, the completion section, and the statements in Sections 3, 4 and 8. Checks I did by hand: the spectral-trace identity for B_{n,J}; the resolvent and semigroup passage (variational strong convergence, then F_t(R_n)); the two-replica tail V_{n,m} (|Q|^2 <= n^{2/3}, the n^{-2/3} cell oscillation, sign-symmetry cross terms, monotonicity in m); every exponent in the escape estimate (17/150, 1/60, 4/75, 18/25, 7/100, 2/75, 9/100, 8/5 > 77/50); the Haar-rotation score identity and its sign (I_i - I_j = E[S F]); the field-rotation bound including the diagonal deletion; and the two quadratic inequalities giving I_i <= 3I/m and Z_i <= CR/m. In Section 6 I recomputed the angular generator (Laplacian of x_i/R and drift theta_i(r_bar - r_i)), checked that the integrating factor cancels all R^{-2} and r_bar terms, and checked the finite constraint identity including the delta mass of L_N'. Also checked: the Laplace scaling D + z L_hat ~ sqrt z (so K ~ t^{-1/2}), the consistency of A_y(0+)=O(1) with f(0)=1/M, the threshold-stop logic, the contraction integrals (beta integrals giving v^{1-2xi} and v^{3/2}), the TV coupling argument, and the measurable point-mass selection. For the replacement step: the ring-likelihood coefficient X_j^h (zeta - t)(-t)^{h-1}, moment matching through order 3, and the Lindeberg exponents n^{(4-k)/6} for k >= 5 and n^{-2} remainder at K=24. Sections 3, 4, 7 and 8 were spot-checked only.
main_claim: For zero-field SK heat-bath dynamics at beta=1, with Gaussian or Rademacher couplings: the stationary autocorrelation A_{n,J}(t) and the quench autocorrelation B_{n,J}(s,t) from uniform spins, scaled by n^{1/3} with times in units n^{2/3}, converge jointly in law (locally uniformly) to (A_g, B_g). Here B_g is built from a unique entrance family h_s^g for the edge semigroup e^{-t c_* H_g} on the conditioned GOE-edge Gaussian measure Pi_g. The family starts from delta_0 in the product topology, and B_g(s,.) -> A_g as s -> infinity.
